pillarForecast.why: Direct control is what he asked for; expect at most one clause of relief, then silence. A 'turn on a dime is weird' relapse (run 20) is possible but unlikely (~10%) now that he has felt the alternative.

Gathering a crowd and setting it off is his own clever/satisfying moment scaled up; the 66px radius means chains still need packing. Small risk that B's 26-30 kills read as automatic later in the session.

In B, a pursuer smashing on a rock he just threaded past dies 30-80px behind him, inside the blast. Labelled 'a pursuer blast', so readable after the fact, but it can feel like his own trap went off in his face.
Blasts hurt him like mines; he asked for one set of rules and proposed 'like a mine'. Expect acceptance with maybe a radius/clarity tweak, not a request for immunity.
Faster, more frequent, from behind, on screen most of the run; with direct control he can out-turn them again (v6 'clever dodging').
Direct control should lift him past sector 3 for the first time since v7, easing the 15-run sector fatigue.

biggestRisk: Pursuer blasts hitting him in B. Pursuers sit on his tail, and the move he likes best (thread close past a rock and let the pursuer hit it) now sets off a blast right behind him. Bots never died to a blast because they don't play that way, but he does. If one of those hits kills him with no visible warning, the payoff turns into 'felt bad', and a single unreadable death has flipped play-again before (run 33).
abVerdict: Prefers B (blasts) clearly, and unlike v8-v10 he'll name it: the blasts are loud, visible and his own idea, so expect praise for a chain on B runs (~75%) and 'no explosions this time?' or 'felt flatter' on at least one A run (~45%), possibly saying 'keep the explosions' by the end. Likely qualifier: one complaint or tweak about a blast hurting him.
